subject: Request: temporary SDK escape-hatch for KeenHealth pilot (routing/prefetch control)
messages:
From: Donna Park To: Tessa Morgan Cc: Logan Wright Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 16:12:00 -0800 Subject: Pilot issue: prefix prefetch + routing causing 2-3s tail spikes Hi Tessa — Quick note from our engineering team running the pilot: when we hit concurrent long-document summarization flows the responses intermittently add 2–3s extra latency for about 1/20th of requests. Our devs traced it to the combination of prefix prefetch + routing-to-variant logic — it looks like some sessions are being routed to the prefetch path, but the kvcache warmup is failing and falling back, which adds latency. We can reproduce and attached logs (repro-logs-keenhealth.txt). For the pilot we need a fast unblock: is there any short-term client-side or API escape-hatch we can use to force low-latency path (disable prefetch or bypass variant routing) just for KeenHealth traffic while engineering lands a saner fix? We'd prefer an opt-in flag on the API or an SDK param we can toggle per-tenant. Timeline: we need something by next Wednesday (2026-12-08) to keep the pilot on schedule. Thanks, Donna Director of Product Engineering KeenHealth --- Attachment: repro-logs-keenhealth.txt (text, 84KB) ---- From: Tessa Morgan To: Donna Park Cc: Logan Wright Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 17:02:00 -0800 Subject: Re: Pilot issue: prefix prefetch + routing causing 2-3s tail spikes Hi Donna — thanks for the detailed repro and timeline. I’ve looped in Logan and the runtime team to see what temporary controls we can expose quickly. Short answer: there are two reasonable short-term pivots we can offer: (1) a tenant-level flag to opt out of prefetch/KV caching, or (2) a routing override header to pin to the low-latency variant. Both are non-ideal long-term but can be engineered as temporary escape-hatches. I’m attaching a draft mutual action plan (map_mutual_action_plan.md) for the pilot changes and proposed rollback criteria. I’ll coordinate scope and timelines with the runtime folks and get an ETA in the next 24 hours. —Tessa Account Executive, Redwood Inference --- From: Logan Wright To: Tessa Morgan , Marissa Cole Cc: Karthik Iyer , Sean Gallagher Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 17:25:00 -0800 Subject: Fwd: Pilot issue: prefix prefetch + routing causing 2-3s tail spikes Team — forwarding KeenHealth repro. They need an operational toggle we can flip for their tenant for the next two weeks while we stabilize. This is high-priority for the pilot and likely upsell motion if we keep schedule. Can platform/runtime say which option is quicker (tenant opt-out vs routing-override header)? Also we need guidance on security/abuse for an override header. Logan Senior Sales Engineer --- From: Marissa Cole To: Logan Wright , Tessa Morgan Cc: Karthik Iyer , Sean Gallagher Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 18:04:00 -0800 Subject: Re: Pilot issue: prefix prefetch + routing causing 2-3s tail spikes Thanks for the context. Quick notes from product/platform perspective: - Tenant-level opt-out: requires a short config path + enforcement inside the routing layer. Low complexity but needs a migration checklist (how it interacts with burst capacity and caching metrics). - Routing-override header: faster to surface (we already accept route hints), but adding an "escape-hatch" header that bypasses prefetch/variant selection has security implications — we must ensure only authenticated calls from a tenant can use it (validated against API key / project id). - Both approaches need metrics toggles and an audit log entry. I'll let Karthik and Sean weigh in on implementation ETA. If we can ship a header toggle as a short-term API param scoped to the project id, that seems quickest. Marissa Product Manager, Redwood Console --- From: Karthik Iyer To: Marissa Cole , Logan Wright , Tessa Morgan Cc: Sean Gallagher Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:15:00 -0800 Subject: RE: Pilot issue: prefix prefetch + routing causing 2-3s tail spikes We dug into the logs Donna attached and reproduced locally. Root cause appears to be race between kvcache warmup and variant fallback when a prefix is long and concurrent sessions spike. The runtime already supports a per-request hint (route_hint) but it can be overridden by our autoscaler routing. Two options and rough ETAs: A) Scoped header override (fast): add header X-Redwood-Escape: prefetch=off or X-Redwood-Routing: low-latency. Server-side validation: only valid when API key/project-id matches an allowlist. Implementation estimate: 2 engineers, ~3 business days to gate, add audit logs, and QA. B) Tenant config opt-out (cleaner): expose project-level setting in control plane that disables prefetch for that tenant. Implementation estimate: 3–4 engineers, ~2 weeks (needs console + flags + migration and observability). Recommendation: ship option A as a temporary escape-hatch scoped to the KeenHealth project id; follow up with B for a durable fix. We will produce server-side audit logs and a short monitoring dashboard for the tenant. Karthik Senior Staff Engineer, Runtime Orchestration --- From: Sean Gallagher To: Karthik Iyer , Marissa Cole , Logan Wright , Tessa Morgan Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -0800 Subject: Re: Pilot issue: prefix prefetch + routing causing 2-3s tail spikes Agree with Karthik. Implementation notes for the escape-hatch header: - Add header: X-Redwood-Escape: prefetch=off;validated=true - Validation: signature check using existing API key -> project-id mapping. Only accept when project_id matches an internal allowlist entry. - Audit: write an immutable audit event with request id, project id, user-agent, and which escape parameters were used. - Metrics: increment a per-tenant counter and emit a short-lived trace sample to Sentry. I can own the server-side change and add audit/metrics. Karthik can help wire the routing short-circuit. I estimate a safe canary by Thursday EOD (2026-12-03) if we prioritize. Sean Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime --- From: Logan Wright To: Donna Park , Tessa Morgan Cc: Karthik Iyer , Sean Gallagher , Marissa Cole Date: Thu, 03 Dec 2026 10:12:00 -0800 Subject: Re: Pilot issue: prefix prefetch + routing causing 2-3s tail spikes Donna — quick update for your team: We will expose a temporary header-based escape-hatch: X-Redwood-Escape: prefetch=off. It is scoped to your project id and requires the API key tied to KeenHealth. Sean will roll out a canary tomorrow and we’ll flip it for your tenant once it’s validated. You can call the API with the header in your pilot runs; we’ll keep audit logs and a short monitoring dashboard. Next steps / timeline: - Wed (12/02)–Thu (12/03): implement and canary (internal). - Fri (12/04): flip for KeenHealth, monitor live for 48 hours. - Week of 12/07: work with product to ship tenant opt-out in control plane as durable fix. Logan Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference --- From: Donna Park To: Logan Wright , Tessa Morgan Cc: Procurement Date: Fri, 04 Dec 2026 09:45:00 -0800 Subject: Re: Pilot issue: prefix prefetch + routing causing 2-3s tail spikes Thanks — that sounds perfect. We’ll stand by to flip the header in our test harness on Friday once you confirm canary green. Appreciate the quick turnaround; attaching a short runbook for our team to follow. Donna Director of Product Engineering KeenHealth --- Attachments referenced in thread: repro-logs-keenhealth.txt; proposed-api-patch.patch; map_mutual_action_plan.md
